decision.summary: A rotten-egg smell from the boiler is a possible gas leak, so this is an emergency even though the tenant called it "not urgent". The tenant was told to leave, not use switches or flames, and call 0800 111 999. Job JOB-101 is raised and HeatRight Ltd (C-11) is assigned for an emergency visit within 24h, with the landlord and P1 escalation ESC-104 notified.

answers.question: What severity is this and why, given the tenant says it is not urgent?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is the odorant for a possible gas leak, and gas smells are emergencies under policy whatever the tenant calls them. An 82-year-old household member is also present, which raises the risk.

answers.question: What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: First: leave the flat with everyone, open windows, don't operate switches, the boiler or flames. Second: call the National Gas Emergency line 0800 111 999 now (999 if anyone is unwell). Third: a Gas Safe engineer is being arranged as an emergency, target within 24h, with the confirmed time to follow. This was sent on WhatsApp as MSG-102.

answers.question: Which actions do you take tonight (job, contractor, escalation, landlord)?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (gas, emergency) linked to R-4801. Assigned HeatRight Ltd (C-11, Gas Safe 550123) for an ASAP visit with a 24h target, and messaged them (MSG-105). Emailed landlord Ben Hartley (MSG-103) that the cost may exceed £300 and that he will be called before approval. Escalated P1 to maintenance (ESC-104). Added a note to P-201 about the vulnerable occupant (NOTE-106).

args.body:
Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as urgent right now, even though it may be nothing. Please do these things now:
1. Open the windows and leave the flat, taking everyone with you, including your flatmate's mum.
2. Don't switch lights or electrical items on or off, don't use the boiler, and don't light any flames or smoking.
3. From outside the property, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away, day or night.
If anyone feels unwell, dizzy or sick, call 999.
Once you're safe, reply here. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer to check the boiler as an emergency and will update you as soon as we have a confirmed time. Our target is to have it looked at within 24 hours.
